biography.plain_text: Marion Rolston Wheaton (1921-2025) was a Canadian nurse and businesswoman. She supplied much of the capital for a joint Saskatchewan retail investment in 1949. In Edmonton, she was later named an incorporator, shareholder and provisional director of First Canadian Casualty Insurance Corporation. She also qualified as a private and commercial pilot.

long_biography.plain_text:
The wages Marion Wheaton retained from hospital work supplied most of the money used when she and her husband bought into a shop in Porcupine Plain, Saskatchewan. She had entered the University of Saskatchewan in 1938 and completed a Bachelor of Science with registered-nursing qualifications. Hospital posts followed at Saskatoon City Hospital and the Royal Columbian Hospital in New Westminster.

After moving to Edmonton in 1961, Wheaton sustained interests that linked professional training, community giving and adventure. Her alma mater's College of Nursing later included her on its roll of philanthropists. She also travelled widely across northern Canada by float plane, an extension of the aviation skills for which she earned several formal qualifications.
